Discussed architecture patterns (VPC peering, private control plane), kernel selection/quantization constraints, KV/prefix caching, routing policies, and reseller/billing models. RidgePoint is interested in both a channel partnership and on-prem integration for regulated clients; next step is a deep technical session and sharing infra diagrams.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Lena Park (AE), Marcus Nguyen (SE) - Redwood; Aisha Khan (CTO), Tom Alvarez (Platform Eng), Priya Mehta (Head of Partnerships), Danielle Ruiz (Network Arch) - RidgePoint

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood Inference. Quick intro, Marcus my solutions engineer is here too. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Aisha: Doing good, thanks. We've been looking at hybrid onramp options, wanted to learn how Redwood might fit with our channel motion.
[00:20] Priya: Hi all, Priya here; partnerships lead at RidgePoint. We're particularly curious about the reseller and billing side, and how tight we can get on latency for enterprise customers.
[00:30] Marcus: Great, thanks. Quick agenda — 1) high-level partner model, 2) technical integration patterns (V P C, peering, private control plane), 3) perf and cost tradeoffs, 4) next steps. Sound okay?
[00:45] Tom: Yep, go ahead.
[00:48] Danielle: Also, I'll chime in on networking — we have strict peering rules and a separate transit for regulated tenants.
[00:55] Lena: Perfect. So to start, a quick snapshot: Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private deploys for VPC/on-prem. For partners like you, we typically support a hybrid onramp where RidgePoint can resell or co-host capacity, and customers can either route to a Redwood dedicated pool or run a private control plane in their V P C.
[01:18] Aisha: When you say "private control plane" — is that fully customer-managed? What remains with Redwood?
[01:25] Marcus: Good question. For Private we ship a control plane that you can run in your VPC; customer controls keys, network, and logs. Redwood can still provide managed runtime updates if you opt in. There are two flavors: a fully air-gapped on-prem package (we've done for regulated fintechs), or a VPC-hosted private control plane with peering to Redwood's runtime for catalog updates and optional telemetry.
[01:50] Tom: And how does model catalog syncing work? Do we pull images or do you stream weights?
[01:56] Marcus: We provide model binaries and a versioned catalog. For private/offline setups we provide a secure transfer process — signed artifacts and sha checks. For VPC-connected setups, there's an encrypted artifact registry you can pull from.
[02:10] Priya: From a partner perspective, what's the margin/commit look like? We need to map to our channel pricing.
[02:17] Lena: We usually propose three tiers: resale of hosted API (rev share), dedicated capacity with committed reservations (discounted month-to-month or annual), and a private deployment licensing model (platform fee + support). We'll send a draft pricing grid.
[02:35] Aisha: Okay. On the technical side, our key constraints: sub-50ms tail latency for conversational agents in certain regions, strict audit logs for SOC2, and KMS integration for customer keys.
[02:48] Marcus: For the sub-50ms target we often recommend a Dedicated pool colocated in the customer's region and model variants that are quantized but tuned for quality. Also: aggressive prefix caching and KV cache to avoid recomputing prompts. Note, latency SLOs depend heavily on sequence length and batching.
[03:10] Tom: When you say "KV cache" sometimes our docs show K V cache spelled out, sorry — just clarifying what you mean by that; are you caching key/value attention states across requests?
[03:20] Marcus: Yes exactly — KV cache is the attention key/value cache. We do prefix caching for common system prompts and can reuse KV segments for repeated user contexts to reduce per-token compute. Works well for chat patterns.
[03:35] Danielle: Network-wise, we need to know whether Redwood will initiate peering or we need to. We also require BGP routing and strict ACLs — some of our tenants will not allow public endpoints even to pull model updates.
[03:50] Marcus: We support both. For peering we can do VPC peering, private link, or an S3-like artifact pull over a private endpoint. For fully air-gapped customers we ship an encrypted artifact bundle that your infra team can import.
[04:05] Priya: Curious about rollout controls — can we do canary deploys per-tenant? Our compliance team wants the ability to limit new model versions to a subset of customers.
[04:15] Lena: Yes, the Redwood Console supports per-route and per-tenant rollouts, canary and A/B testing, and automatic fallbacks to a fallback model if latency or error rates spike.
[04:26] Aisha: Good. On security: SSO, SAML for user access to the console, RBAC by team, and audit logs — are those built-in?
[04:33] Marcus: Built-in. We have SAML/SSO integrations, fine-grained RBAC, and audit logs. For Private deployments, logs can be routed to your ELK/splunk or to our hosted analytics depending on the setup — customers often prefer to keep logs in their tenancy for regulated workloads.
[04:50] Tom: What about KMS/HSM integration? We need BYOK for model keys and token encryption.
[04:56] Marcus: We integrate with cloud KMS services and support HSM for private customers. Keys never leave the customer's HSM on the private control plane.
[05:06] Priya: Switching gear — how does routing and smart fallback work when capacity is constrained? If a customer calls our endpoint and your Dedicated pool is saturated, do you failover to hosted?
[05:18] Marcus: There are routing policies. You can route by latency, cost, or region. We support automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in another pool or to a lower-tier hosted model. Policies are configurable per-customer or per-route.
[05:34] Aisha: We have some customers with very specific quantization requirements — can't accept certain fp16 conversions. How do you manage kernel selection and quantized variants?
[05:44] Marcus: The runtime performs kernel selection based on architecture, hardware, and sequence length distribution. For quantization we support multiple profiles; you can pin a tenant to a model variant/precision that meets your quality bar. We also offer eval tooling to benchmark quality regressions before rollout.
[06:05] Tom: Does the runtime expose metrics for token-level latency and cost breakdown? Our billing engine needs token-level chargebacks for tenants.
[06:13] Lena: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdowns and per-route traces. For partners/resellers we can provide a reporting API you can pull into your billing system.
[06:26] Danielle: We'll need to verify egress and ingress requirements for the dedicated pools. Do you require NAT or can we do static internal routing?
[06:34] Marcus: You can run the runtime in routable subnets with internal IPs; NAT isn't strictly required if peering and proper routes are in place. We'll share a networking checklist.
[06:47] Priya: On the channel contractual side, can partners manage customer onboarding or is Redwood the point of contact for support?
[06:55] Lena: We do flexible partner enablement: partners can be the primary onboarding and support contact, or Redwood can handle first-line support with escalation to partner. We also offer partner training and co-branded docs.
[07:08] Aisha: Cost sensitivity: for some workloads we need the cheapest per-token cost even at the expense of higher latency; for others it's the opposite. Can you support mixed routing rules so we can optimize per-customer?
[07:20] Marcus: Yes — routing policies per route/tenant so you can choose cost-first or latency-first. We also provide Optimize tooling that recommends batching, quantization, and cache settings per workload.
[07:34] Tom: About benchmarking — if we want to run benchmarks on our infra, what do you need from us?
[07:40] Marcus: We'll need a sample model (or pick a model from our catalog), a representative prompt set, and the target percentiles you care about (p50/p90/p99). Also access to a test endpoint or a staging Dedicated pool. We'll run continuous batching sims and KV cache scenarios.
[07:58] Danielle: Network team will need to understanding egress ports and certificate rotation processes.
[08:05] Marcus: We'll include those details in the networking checklist and the runbook for cert rotation.
[08:12] Priya: Any restrictions around resale in certain regions? We operate across NA and EU and some APAC for select customers.
[08:20] Lena: We support regional deployments; data residency can be managed via Dedicated or Private deployments. Licensing varies by region but we're used to EU/NA partnerships and can discuss APAC on a case-by-case basis.
[08:34] Aisha: Can we get a quick example flow for a regulated tenant — say they want on-prem model serving but still want Redwood to push security updates — how does that operate?
[08:44] Marcus: That would be the VPC-hosted private control plane: you run the control plane in your VPC, we ship signed updates which your infra team approves or we can do zero-touch if you opt in. For on-prem air-gapped, we provide artifact bundles and a guide for offline patching.
[09:03] Tom: And telemetry — does Redwood collect model usage telemetry by default? For regulated customers we need opt-in telemetry only.
[09:11] Marcus: Telemetry is opt-in; for Private runs you keep telemetry internal. For Dedicated/reseller flows we can provide aggregated metrics to Redwood for billing but not raw PII.
[09:25] Priya: Any gotchas around multi-tenancy? We run multiple tenants per cluster; need strong isolation.
[09:31] Marcus: We support per-tenant isolation via namespaces and per-tenant KV prefixes, and the runtime enforces resource quotas. For strict regulatory tenants we recommend dedicated nodes or dedicated pools.
[09:46] Danielle: From a connectivity standpoint, we may need to require IP allowlists that are ephemeral — how do you manage IP churn for your hosted endpoints?
[09:55] Marcus: For hosted endpoints we publish a range of egress IPs and support private link for static connectivity. For Dedicated we can provide static IPs in your VPC.
[10:07] Lena: Quick pause — does any of this feel out of scope for RidgePoint's current priorities?
[10:12] Aisha: No, mostly aligned. The main ask is to validate perf with our models and to see the networking checklist.
[10:20] Marcus: Understood. I'll prepare a perf plan.
[10:23] Priya: Also, can you outline the partner enablement — playbooks for our sales and support teams?
[10:29] Lena: Yes, partner enablement kit includes playbooks, co-branded docs, and training sessions. We'll share a draft.
[10:36] Tom: Any experience with GPU vendors for onramp? We currently work with both Ampere and A100 fleets, a mix.
[10:43] Marcus: We've integrated with both Ampere and Nvidia A100/A800 families. Kernel selection handles instruction differences; we recommend model-specific tuning. If you have a mix, we can map model variants to hardware classes.
[10:58] Danielle: Do you do quantized int8 workflows and how mature are they? We need to know the expected quality delta.
[11:06] Marcus: Yes int8 quantization is supported. We provide quantization profiles and an eval harness to measure quality regression. For many workloads, int8 is within acceptable bounds but evaluate per-model.
[11:20] Priya: On the business model — is there an opportunity for co-selling or joint go-to-market?
[11:25] Lena: Definitely. We typically set a co-sell motion for channel partners: joint marketing, lead sharing, and deal registration with tiered margins. We can tailor based on ARR commitments.
[11:40] Aisha: The timeline: some of our customers want pilots within 6-8 weeks. Is that feasible?
[11:49] Marcus: Yes, for a pilot we can provision a staging dedicated pool or spin up a private control plane; typical lead time depends on capacity and infra approvals but 6 weeks is realistic for a standard pilot.
[12:00] Tom: If we do a pilot, what telemetry and SLAs come with it?
[12:06] Lena: Pilots come with basic observability, token-level cost dashboards, and a pilot SLA for availability. For production we discuss enterprise SLAs.
[12:16] Danielle: Let's talk about certification and audits — if our customers ask for SOC2 attestation for the partner-managed flow, do you provide that for the dedicated infrastructure?
[12:26] Marcus: Redwood maintains SOC2; for Private or Dedicated you can configure where logs live for audit. We'll share our compliance pack.
[12:35] Priya: Are there minimum commit sizes for Dedicated? Some partners balk at large GPU reservations.
[12:42] Lena: We offer both monthly and annual commit options; minimums are negotiable depending on partner tier. We'll propose a few options in the pricing grid.
[12:54] Aisha: Any sample case study of a reseller who integrated this way?
[12:58] Lena: Yes — we worked with a channel partner in fintech where they resold dedicated capacity and managed on-boarding for regulated tenants. I'll share a short case study.
[13:08] Marcus: I'll follow up with technical notes about kernel selection, quant profiles, and the perf benchmark template.
[13:15] Tom: Good. Also side question — how do you handle large model artifacts for initial sync? We have slow links to some zones.
[13:23] Marcus: For constrained networks we do manifest-based delta sync and can ship a physical appliance for extreme cases.
[13:32] Danielle: Appreciate that.
[13:35] Priya: Anything else from your side?
[13:38] Marcus: One more technical note — when you run in mixed-hardware clusters, you may need placement constraints; we expose placement tags so you can target A100 vs Ampere.
[13:50] Aisha: That helps.
[13:52] Lena: Okay — let's recap next steps. We'll send: 1) partner integration spec + pricing tiers, 2) networking checklist & cert rotation runbook, 3) perf benchmark template and request for sample prompts/model, 4) partner enablement kit and case study.
[14:14] Priya: That sounds good. We'll share infra diagrams and peering contacts by next week.
[14:20] Danielle: I'll coordinate with Tom on the network details.
[14:23] Tom: Thanks.
[14:25] Aisha: Quick nit — can Marcus include an estimated cost per token for int8 vs fp16 for a 2k-token convo? Ballpark is fine.
[14:33] Marcus: Yes — I'll include ballparks in the follow-up along with the perf plan assumptions.
[14:39] Priya: Great. Anything else?
[14:41] Lena: No — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc pack.
[14:45] Aisha: Thanks.
[14:47] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional transcription artifacts (V P C, K V cache spelled out) present. References: Partner deck (shared link): https://rwd.redwood/decks/ridgepoint-onramp | Networking checklist (to be shared)

End of transcript.
